research_payload.counter_arguments: Boundary dispute: Lafayette class vs. separate James Madison/Benjamin Franklin classes. Some sources list James Madison (SSBN-627 to 636) and Benjamin Franklin (SSBN-640 to 645) as distinct classes; NHHC and most authoritative sources treat as subgroups of Lafayette class with minor improvements. Decision: combined under Lafayette to avoid padding roster with near-identical variants per DvsU guidance. Boundary dispute: Ohio SSGN conversions. Four Ohio-class boats converted to cruise missile role 2002-2008; some sources list as separate SSGN class. Decision: noted within Ohio class entry as conversions, not separate class. Boundary dispute: Columbia class inclusion. Lead boat under construction (65% complete Feb 2026) but not commissioned as of 2026. Decision: excluded because 'Ever Built' title for submarines means commissioned submarines; delivery expected 2028, first patrol 2031. Boundary dispute: Jack SSN-605 as separate class. Initial validation finding suggested missing class; research verified Jack as Permit-class member with experimental contra-rotating propellers, not separate class. Decision: included in Thresher/Permit class roster. Boundary dispute: Tullibee SSN-597 as separate class vs. variant. Single-ship experimental design; decision: included as distinct class because commissioned with unique propulsion system (turbo-electric drive) and configuration (bow sonar, amidships torpedo tubes).

payload.fact_sheet: ROSTER DISCOVERY PASS - Full enrichment deferred. Classes verified: Holland SS-1 (1 boat, 1900) through Virginia SSN-799 (26 boats commissioned through April 2026). Jack SSN-605 confirmed as Permit-class member. Columbia SSBN-826 excluded as under construction, not commissioned. independent_coverage_audit.summary: AUDIT FAILED. The roster contains a fundamental classification error that violates the 'every class ever built' scope: it splits the single Plunger class (7 submarines, SS-2 through SS-8, all commissioned 1903) into two separate classes - 'Plunger class' (1 boat) and 'Adder class' (5 boats, though roster lists only 5 member units when there should be 6 remaining boats). NHHC and GlobalSecurity definitively confirm these are one class of 7 submarines, later redesignated A-1 through A-7. The roster's stated boundary claims 'all commissioned USN submarine classes' but artificially inflates the count by splitting a single class. Additionally, the AA-1/T-class situation requires clarification: the WWI-era AA-1 class (3 submarines, SS-52/60/61, commissioned 1920-1922) was renamed T-class, but the roster lists 'T-1 class' as 1953 training submarines, suggesting either a missing WWI class or misidentification of a post-WWII program. The scope_conforms=false because the roster's own classification contradicts authoritative naval records on what constitutes distinct classes.

findings.problem: These are the SAME class. NHHC and multiple authoritative sources confirm the Plunger class comprised 7 submarines (SS-2 through SS-8): Plunger, Adder, Moccasin, Porpoise, Shark, Grampus, and Pike. The roster incorrectly splits this single 7-boat class into 'Plunger class' (1 boat) and 'Adder class' (5 boats), inflating the class count. The class is sometimes called 'Adder class' because USS Adder was first completed, but it is one class, not two.

The roster appears to confuse the WWI-era T-class (AA-1 class) with a different post-WWII designation or has misidentified a training submarine program.
